Commentary.Commentary: That's all from this game! However, we have another game coming up at the same ground. It is between South Africa Women and West Indies Women. It is still pouring down at the ground and it looks unlikely that we will have a prompt start. Let's keep our fingers crossed. Do join us for that game. Until then, cheers.

Javeria Khan, the Pakistan skipper says Maroof has had a surgery and she hopes that she recovers quickly. Further adds Thailand's batting surprised them and it gave them a lesson that you should never be complacent. Further adds that she congratulates Thailand for playing fearless cricket. Mentions Diana and Nida did bowl decently but they could not execute their plans here. Ends by saying that they will head back with their heads held high, they played well but made mistakes at important times.

Sornnarin Tippoch, the Thailand skipper says they had a positive mindset today and the openers did really well. Further adds this was the last game and so they wanted to play aggressive cricket. Mentions she is pleased they played at this stage and they want to play more against the big side. Reckons the people back home will be very happy and they will be an example for the youngsters. She ends by saying they will prepare for the next World Cup and come stronger.

So, a sad end to the journey for Thailand in this Women's World Cup. They batted well to reach their highest ever T20I score and it was Nattaka Kancham who led from the front with a fifty. She and Nattaya Boochatham stitched a 93-run stand to give them a good start. They eventually ended up with 150 on the board which looked a very good score on this wicket. Pakistan, on the other hand, were poor with the ball. They kept on bowling full tosses and they were rightly put away. Anam Amin was disappointing, while Nida Dar was the pick of the bowlers, bowling economically as well as picking up a wicket. Their batters had a tough job on their hands as they had never chased a total above 150 but the Rain Gods saved them as it started pouring down at the end of the first innings. Stay tuned for the presentation ceremony...
UPDATE 1757 LOCAL (0657 GMT) - The inevitable has happened as the rain has failed to relent and the game has been CALLED OFF.

UPDATE 1743 LOCAL (0643 GMT) - Nothing new to update as it is still raining at the moment. Let's keep our fingers crossed that we have a game resumption soon. The cut-off time for a 5-over game is 1803 Local (0703 GMT).

We have started to lose overs also. There is no movement on the ground as of now as the players have also moved from their dugout to their dressing rooms.

Anjum Chopra is down with the two umpires. Clair Polosak says that the rain has got heavier at the end of the first innings. Mentions that they have 30 mins of time before they start losing overs. She says that they would look to get the maximum they can get from the game. Chris Brown further says that for now they are just keeping a close eye on the weather and he hopes that it clears sooner than later but for now the covers stay firmly onto the pitch.

Ohh no!!! It has started raining and the covers are coming onto the pitch. This is not something that Thailand would have wanted as they batted well and would be itching to have a crack at the Pakistani batters. Let's hope that the rain clears away.

So, the target for Pakistan is 151 in the 20 overs. Their batters will need to bat responsibly and with intent if they have to win it here and end the tournament with a high. Thailand would hope that their bowlers come good and restrict Pakistan to win their first game in this tournament. Will we see Thailand cause an upset or will Pakistan prevail? Do join us shortly for the chase on the other side of the break.
Nattaka Chantam says that she is happy to have batted like this. Adds that she just followed the plans and she did her job. Goes onto say that she has enjoyed the World Cup.

Talking of the Pakistan bowling, they were not as their usual self as Diana Baig their best bowler so far in the tournament was smashed all around the park. Anam Amin, Aliya Riaz too failed to contain the run flow. Only Nida Dar looked somewhat in the groove as she kept the Thailand batters quiet for sometime. Overall, Pakistan would not be happy with their poor bowling and also some shoddy fielding. Meanwhile, Nattakan Chantam is down for a quick chat with Anjum Chopra.

What a batting performance we have seen from Thailand! They just played like there is no other day. It started with the toss when Sornnarin Tippoch, the Thailand skipper, after winning the toss, to everyone's surprise opted to bat first. Their openers were spot on from the word go. Nattakan Chantam and Nattaya Boochatham were firing on all cylinders. The pair added 93 runs for the opening wicket. The duo took on Pakistan bowling as all their bowlers were sent on a leather hunt. Though Nattaya Boochatham missed out on a well-deserved fifty but her partner Nattakan Chantam got to hers. In the end, Thailand ended with 150 runs on the board, their highest T20I score.

The rain has eased out and we are all set to begin on time! The Pakistan players are making their way out to the middle, after being in a huddle. They are followed by Nattakan Chantam and Nattaya Boochatham. Diana Baig will start with the ball.
Both the teams are making their way out to the field to stand in respect for their respective National Anthems.
There is a bit of rain falling and the pitch has been covered. Let's hope that we have a start on time.
Pitch report - Ebony Rainford-Brent is there for the pitch report. She says that the pitch is a bit firm and there will be good carry on this surface.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Muneeba Ali, Javeria Khan (c), Umaima Sohail, Nida Dar, Aliya Riaz, Sidra Nawaz (wk), Iram Javed, Syeda Aroob Shah, Ayesha Naseem (DEBUT, IN FOR AIMAN ANWER), Diana Baig, Anam Amin.

Thailand (Unchanged Playing XI) - Nattakan Chantam, Nattaya Boochatham, Nannapat Koncharoenkai (wk), Naruemol Chaiwai, Chanida Sutthiruang, Sornnarin Tippoch (c), Wongpaka Liengprasert, Onnicha Kamchomphu, Ratanaporn Padunglerd, Suleeporn Laomi, Soraya Lateh.

Javeria khan, Pakistan skipper says that they would have bowled first looking at the conditions. Further says that they would look to restrict them and chase it down. Mentions that the girls have been superb with their performance. Further says that they are all missing Bismah but her job is to enjoy batting and give confidence to the youngsters.

Sonnarin Tippoch, Thailand skipper says that they will bat first. She says that they want to set a score and then defend it. Further says that they want to execute their plans while bowling. Mentions that they have enjoyed their journey in the entire tournament.
TOSS - It's time for the the flip of the coin. Up goes the coin and it lands in favour of Sornnarin Tippoch. THAILAND HAVE ELECTED TO BAT FIRST!

Greetings! A warm welcome to the final day of the group stages. It is Pakistan facing Thailand in the first game of the double-header Tuesday. Both teams are out of the race for the semi-finals and they would be looking to play for pride. Thailand have lost all their three games and would be hoping that they end the competition with a win. They need to improve their bowling and fielding in order to achieve that. Pakistan, on the other hand, started the tournament well but fizzled out in their last two games to bow out of the competition. They will look to finish on a high. Toss and team updates in a while.
